observations: All three photos show a shop front with large stacks of used tires piled under a tin roof, multiple tires visible with differing tread patterns and markings (colored chalk marks, no legible brand or size).
No single tire is isolated or photographed close-up; these appear to be general inventory/stock shots, not a photo of the specific tire being sold.
No sidewall text, brand name, size code, or DOT date is readable in any photo.
No tread-depth gauge, ruler, or close-up of a specific tire's tread is shown.
No photo shows the inside of any tire (where patches or bulges would be visible) or a close-up confirming 'no patch, no bulge'.

claims.evidence: No business signage, distributor certificate, or brand marking visible in any photo; 'Belgium tires' is a generic Nigerian market term, not a verifiable brand from these shots.

claims.claim: Tread is still 90 percent, no patch, no bulge
claims.evidence: No close-up of the specific tire's tread, no gauge/ruler shown, and no inside-tire shot to check for patches or bulges; photos show a general stock pile, not the item itself.
No DOT date code or any identifying mark legible in photos 0-2.

risks.proof: A close-up photo of the exact tire for sale, showing full tread circumference and sidewall.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic used tire of unknown/lower grade

risks.risk: Tread depth claim (90%) cannot be confirmed without measurement.
risks.proof: Photo of tread with a gauge or coin for scale.

risks.proof: Photo of the inner sidewall and inside tread surface of the specific tire.

risks.risk: Tire size and actual brand unverified, affecting fitment and value.

proof_requests: Photo of the exact tire being sold, isolated from the stack, showing full sidewall and size/brand text.
Close-up of tread with a depth gauge or coin for scale.
Photo of the inner sidewall and inside tread to confirm no patch or bulge.
Photo of the DOT/date code on the sidewall to verify age.
response.reason: The item is identifiable only as a generic used tire; none of the seller's claims (grade, tread %, origin, year) are shown or verifiable in the photos, so it must be priced at the low, unverified-grade end of the comparable market rather than the 'first grade' or premium-labeled listings.
